correctness.rationale: Exact Zak multiplier gives positive essential spectral bounds. The evaluated leverage equals \(1/q\); rank-one positivity and essential-spectrum stability yield a unique discrete eigenvalue exactly when the integrable edge resolvent exceeds one. Direct logarithmic angular asymptotics give \(E_q(a)\sim1/(q\sqrt{\pi a})\) as \(a\downarrow0\) and \(E_q(a)\to1/q+1/2\) as \(a\to\infty\) for each fixed integer \(q\). The included numerical script checks formulas but is not an infinite-dimensional proof. The case \(q=2\) is not used to infer a two-phase transition.

value.rationale: The sharp reconstruction constant after losing one sample is a motivated frame-theoretic invariant beyond mere frame survival. The explicit Cauchy threshold identifies a real shift from no spectral loss to appearance of a discrete eigenvalue below the original continuous band; the pole-depth limits rigorously show both regimes at every fixed integer oversampling \(q\ge3\). This does not follow by restating general excess or positive-frame criteria.
